notes: Same as Girls State — prestigious civic program. Rising junior should seek nomination in spring. CT program is well-regarded.; [DEAD: https://www.legion.org/boysstate]

name: National Youth Science Camp (NYSC) — Alumni Scholarship
eligibility: NYSC alumni
notes: Secondary scholarship available after attending NYSC.; [DEAD: https://www.nyscamp.org/alumni/scholarships/]

name: The U.S. Senate Youth Program (USSYP)
eligibility: High school juniors (rising seniors), US citizens, elected student government officer or demonstrate leadership
aid: $10,000 college scholarship + all-expenses-paid trip to Washington DC
notes: Extremely prestigious. CT delegates are selected through a state-level competition. Rising junior should seek student government positions. Application typically opens in September of junior year. Good for law/civics interest.

name: CT State Scholarships — New England Board of Higher Education (NEBHE)
eligibility: CT residents attending certain programs at public New England colleges
notes: CT residents can get tuition breaks at public colleges in ME, NH, VT, RI, MA for certain programs. Check NEBHE website for participating programs in biology/law.
source: New England Board of Higher Education

name: India Club of Greater St. Louis — Indian American Scholarship
eligibility: Indian American high school seniors, St. Louis area residents
notes: CT-based Indian American students should look for similar organizations in CT/Northeast: India Cultural Society, Federation of Indian Associations (FIA) of New England, TiE Boston, etc.; [DEAD: https://www.indiaclubofstl.org/scholarship/]
source: India Club of Greater St. Louis

name: TiE (The Indus Entrepreneurs) Scholarships
eligibility: Varies by chapter; often open to South Asian students or students interested in entrepreneurship
notes: Search for TiE Connecticut or TiE Boston for local scholarship programs. Also TiE Young Entrepreneurs (TYE) program for high school students interested in business/entrepreneurship.; [DEAD: https://www.tie.org/education/]

name: Federation of Indian Associations (FIA) of New England Scholarships
eligibility: Indian American high school students in New England
notes: Regional Indian American organization. Check website for scholarship announcements, typically in spring. CT-based Indian American students are within the New England region.; [DEAD: https://www.fianewengland.org/]
source: Federation of Indian Associations of New England

name: Connecticut Association of Latinos in Higher Education (CALAHE) Scholarships
eligibility: Hispanic/Latino students, CT residents
notes: Not applicable.

name: Society of Professional Journalists Scholarships
eligibility: High school seniors and college students pursuing journalism careers
notes: More relevant if student has a journalism or writing interest. Multiple scholarships available through SPJ.; [DEAD: https://www.spj.org/scholarships.asp]

name: Southern Connecticut State University Scholarships
eligibility: CT high school students, varies by scholarship
notes: University-specific merit scholarships. Check SCSU for specific programs relevant to biology/pre-law.; [DEAD: https://www.southernct.edu/admissions/financial-aid/scholarships]

name: University of Connecticut Merit Scholarships
eligibility: Incoming UConn freshmen, CT residents (most scholarships), strong academic record
notes: UConn offers strong programs in biology (College of Agriculture, Health and Natural Resources) and pre-law. Many merit scholarships are awarded automatically based on admissions application.; [DEAD: https://admissions.uconn.edu/merit-scholarships/]

name: National Italian American Foundation (NIAF) Scholarships
eligibility: Italian American students
notes: Not applicable.

name: Asian American Foundation (TAAF) Scholarships
eligibility: Asian American students
notes: TAAF is relatively new (founded 2021). Check for scholarship programs. Primarily focused on community support and anti-Asian hate initiatives.

name: Paul & Daisy Soros Fellowships for New Americans
eligibility: Immigrants or children of immigrants (green card holders, naturalized citizens), pursuing graduate study, ages 30 and under
notes: Not applicable now but worth knowing about for the future. Child of Indian immigrants (first-generation American) qualifies under 'New Americans' criteria.
source: Paul & Daisy Soros Fellowships for New Americans

name: Jack Kent Cooke Young Artist Award
eligibility: High school students with financial need and artistic talent
notes: Not applicable.; [DEAD: https://www.jkcf.org/our-scholarships/young-artist-award/]

name: The All American Youth Foundation Scholarships
eligibility: Varies by program
notes: Check for current scholarship programs. Some may target first-generation college students.

name: The Barry Goldwater Scholarship
eligibility: College sophomores and juniors, US citizens/permanent residents, STEM majors (including biology), strong research interest
notes: Future opportunity for biology-focused student. Requires research experience and faculty nomination in college. Rising junior should think about undergrad plans with research components.

name: The Udall Foundation Scholarship
eligibility: College sophomores and juniors, US citizens/permanent residents
notes: Future opportunity if student develops environmental biology interest.; [DEAD: https://www.udall.gov/scholarship.aspx]

name: The Princeton Prize in Race Relations
eligibility: High school students (grades 9-12), US residents, demonstrated work in race relations
notes: Excellent for law-interested student with passion for race relations. The Indian American experience could be a compelling subject. CT has a regional award committee.; [DEAD: https://pprr.princeton.edu/]

name: The Stamps Scholarship
eligibility: Incoming freshmen at partner universities, exceptional academic and leadership record
aid: Full tuition, fees, room, board + enrichment fund ($10,000–$20,000)
notes: Excellent merit scholarship for high-achieving students. Partner universities include many top schools. Rising junior should research which partner universities offer Stamps Scholarships and their criteria.; [DEAD: https://www.stampsfoundation.org/]

name: The Robertson Scholars Program
eligibility: High school seniors, US citizens/permanent residents, exceptional leadership and character
aid: Full tuition, room, board, fees + summer enrichment (value ~$300,000+)
notes: One of the most generous merit scholarships. Good fit for students with strong leadership. Rising junior should focus on developing leadership and service record.

name: The Gates Cambridge Scholarship
eligibility: Graduate study applicants, non-UK, intellectual and leadership excellence
aid: Full cost of graduate study at Cambridge (tuition, fees, living, travel)
notes: Not applicable now. Future opportunity.

name: Children of Fallen Patriots Foundation
eligibility: Children of fallen military service members
notes: Not applicable.

name: The Boettcher Foundation Scholarship (Colorado)
eligibility: Colorado high school seniors, CO residents
notes: Not applicable geographically.

name: The Enterprise Holdings Foundation Scholarship
eligibility: Varies by program
notes: Varies by year. Check for new programs.; [URL may block bots: https://www.enterpriseholdings.com/enterprise-holdings-foundation/]

name: The Ritchie-Jennings Memorial Scholarship (ACFE)
eligibility: Undergraduate/graduate students in accounting, business, or criminal justice
notes: Not a strong fit for this profile.

name: The National Parents Council Scholarships
eligibility: Varies by program
notes: Not well-known; verify current program status.; [DEAD: https://www.pcscholarship.org/]

eligibility: South Carolina residents
notes: Not applicable.; [DEAD: https://www.josephpriley.org/]

notes: Not applicable.

eligibility: American Indian/Alaska Native students
notes: Not applicable.

name: The Society of Asian Scientists and Engineers (SASE) Scholarships
eligibility: Asian American students, US citizens/permanent residents, pursuing STEM careers
notes: SASE has active conferences and networking opportunities. Good fit for Indian American student with biology interest.
source: Society of Asian Scientists and Engineers

name: National Association of Asian American Professionals (NAAAP) Scholarships
eligibility: Asian American high school seniors, US citizens/permanent residents
notes: NAAAP has a national presence with local chapters. Check for CT chapter. Multiple scholarship opportunities available annually.
source: National Association of Asian American Professionals

name: The DAR (Daughters of the American Revolution) Scholarships
eligibility: US citizens, high school seniors or college students, varies by scholarship
notes: DAR offers multiple scholarship categories. Check for scholarships in CT. Some are for specific majors or interests.

name: The American Society of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology (ASBMB) Scholarships
eligibility: Undergraduate students in biochemistry/molecular biology
notes: Future opportunity for biology-focused student after starting college.; [DEAD: https://www.asbmb.org/career-resources/undergraduate-scholarships]
source: American Society of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology

name: The American Physiological Society (APS) Undergraduate Summer Fellowships
eligibility: Undergraduate students in physiology/biology
notes: Future opportunity for college student interested in biology research.; [DEAD: https://www.physiology.org/career/undergraduate/]

name: The National Institute of Health (NIH) Summer Internship Program (SIP)
eligibility: High school students (age 17+ at start), college students, US citizens/permanent residents, strong academic record
notes: Excellent biology research opportunity. NIH is in Bethesda, MD (requires travel from CT). Rising junior should prepare strong academic record and get research experience. The stipend covers housing/food.

name: The National Merit Scholarship — PSAT/NMSQT Preparation
eligibility: All US high school students in 11th grade (and some 10th graders), US citizens/permanent residents
cost: Free (PSAT/NMSQT registration fee ~$18, may be waived by school)
notes: The PSAT/NMSQT is the single most important step for National Merit. Rising junior should start PSAT practice in summer before 11th grade. Khan Academy offers free practice through College Board partnership.; [DEAD: https://www.nationalmerit.org/psat-nmsqt]
source: National Merit Scholarship Corporation / College Board

name: College Board National Recognition Programs
eligibility: US citizens/permanent residents, GPA 3.5+, PSAT/NMSQT scores in top 10% of region, and meet one of: African American, Hispanic/Latino, Indigenous, rural/small-town, or first-generation
aid: Recognition program (not direct cash) — strengthens college applications and may lead to scholarship offers
notes: The First-Generation Recognition program could apply if parents immigrated and do not hold US bachelor's degrees. This recognition can strengthen college applications and scholarship chances.; [DEAD: https://bigfuture.collegeboard.org/scholarships-and-grants/national-recognition-programs]

name: The KPMG Future Leaders Scholarship
eligibility: High school seniors, diverse background, pursuing business related degrees
notes: Not a strong fit.; [DEAD: https://www.kpmgfoundation.com/]

name: The Kohler Co. Scholarship Program
eligibility: Children of Kohler employees
notes: Company-specific. Check if parents' employers offer similar scholarships.

name: The Mensa Education & Research Foundation Scholarships
eligibility: High school seniors and college students, US citizens/permanent residents
notes: Essay-based scholarship. No income restriction. Good for law-interested student with writing ability.

name: The National Center for Women & Information Technology (NCWIT) Award for Aspirations in Computing
eligibility: Female, transgender, or non-binary high school students interested in computing/technology
notes: Only relevant if student has computing/technology interest alongside biology.
source: National Center for Women & Information Technology

name: The International Science and Engineering Fair (ISEF) Awards
eligibility: High school students, must qualify through affiliated science fair
notes: Excellent for biology research. CT students compete through the Connecticut Science Fair (affiliated with ISEF). Rising junior should develop a research project and enter the CT Science Fair.

name: The President's Environmental Youth Award (PEYA)
eligibility: K-12 students, US residents, completed environmental project
notes: Good for biology/environment interest. Recognition can strengthen other scholarship applications.

name: The National FFA Scholarships
eligibility: FFA members, high school students, pursuing agriculture/STEM careers
notes: Only relevant if student is involved in FFA/agriculture. CT has active FFA chapters.

name: The Optometry Glaucoma Scholarship
eligibility: Optometry students
notes: Not applicable.; [DEAD: https://www.optometryglaucoma.org/]

name: The American Chemical Society (ACS) Scholarships
eligibility: Underrepresented minority students pursuing chemistry-related degrees, US citizens/permanent residents, high school seniors or college students
notes: Check ACS Scholars Program criteria for Indian American eligibility. Some years include Asian Americans as underrepresented in chemistry, others don't. Call to confirm.

name: The American Society for Microbiology (ASM) Scholarships
eligibility: Undergraduate/graduate students in microbiology
notes: Future opportunity for biology-focused student.

name: National Geographic Society Young Explorers Grants
eligibility: Ages 18-25, project-based proposal
notes: Future opportunity for biology/environment interest.

name: The Earth Science Week Contest (American Geosciences Institute)
eligibility: K-12 students, varies by category
notes: Minor contest, not a major scholarship. Good for building a portfolio of awards.

name: The Actuarial Foundation Scholarships
eligibility: Students pursuing actuarial science careers
notes: Not a strong fit for this profile.

name: The Future of STEM Scholars Initiative (FOSSI)
eligibility: Underrepresented minority students, HBCU-bound, STEM majors
notes: Not applicable.; [DEAD: https://www.fossischolars.org/]

name: USA Biology Olympiad (USABO)
eligibility: Grades 9-12; US citizens or legal permanent residents
cost: $125/school registration fee (covers all students from that school)
aid: No need-based aid; travel and accommodation for National Finals covered by sponsors
notes: School must register first ($125 fee) before students can register. Open Exam administered via AoPS in February 2027 for the 2027 cycle. Registration opens August 1, 2026 for the 2027 USABO cycle. Strongly recommended for students interested in biology/medicine. Extremely prestigious - top finishers get significant admissions boost.

name: AMC 8 (American Mathematics Competition - Grade 8)
eligibility: Grade 8 and below; age under 15.5 on competition day
cost: $55 early bird (by Oct 28, 2026), $75 regular (by Jan 5, 2027), $115 late (by Jan 14, 2027) per school; plus $25 per 10-student bundle
aid: No individual financial aid; school-level registration
notes: Early Bird Registration Deadline: Oct 28, 2026. Regular: Jan 5, 2027. Late: Jan 14, 2027 (returning managers only). Competition date: Jan 21-27, 2027. Gateway to AIME, USAMO, and IMO team selection. Indian American and Asian American students are heavily represented at top levels.

name: AIME (American Invitational Mathematics Examination)
eligibility: Top ~2.5% of AMC 12 scorers and top ~5% of AMC 10 scorers. By invitation only.
cost: No direct cost; school registers qualified students
notes: AIME I: February 2027. AIME II: February 2027 (alternate date). Score on AIME combined with AMC score determines USAMO/JMO qualification. Extremely prestigious for college admissions.

name: BioGENEius Challenge
eligibility: Grades 9-12. US high school students. CT falls under At-Large category (not a state partner state).
aid: Travel support for finalists to attend BioFuture Conference
notes: Research-based competition - student must have original biotech research. Application includes project poster (PDF) and authorization forms. International component also available. 2024 challenge was held October 28-30 in NYC. 2026 details pending - check website. Ideal for biology-focused students with research.

name: National Science Bowl (NSB)
deadline: Varies by region (typically October-January for regional registration)
eligibility: Grades 9-12. Teams of 4-5 students (with alternates) from same school. US citizenship not required.
aid: Travel to National Finals for winning regional teams is DOE-sponsored
notes: Regional competitions held January-March. National Finals in Washington DC (late April/early May). DOE covers travel and lodging for national finalists. Fast-paced buzzer format. Excellent for biology with broad science coverage. No cost to participate.

name: Junior Science and Humanities Symposium (JSHS)
eligibility: Grades 9-12. US citizens or permanent residents. Must present original research.
aid: Travel to regional and national symposia fully covered. National winners receive scholarships ($4k-$12k).
notes: Regional deadlines usually November-January. Students submit research paper and prepare oral presentation. CT regional symposium typically at University of Connecticut or other regional host. Excellent for biology research students. DoD sponsorship but no military obligation.

name: USA Computing Olympiad (USACO)
deadline: Rolling (4 contests per year: Dec, Jan, Feb, US Open in March)
eligibility: Any pre-college student worldwide. No age/grade restrictions.
notes: Four online contests per year (usually 3-5 days each). December, January, February, and US Open (March). Top US students in Platinum division invited to IOI training camp. Very strong for college admissions. Requires programming knowledge (C++, Java, Python). Not biology but complements STEM profile. Indian American students heavily represented.

name: Genius Olympiad
deadline: Varies (typically April-May for the June event)
eligibility: Grades 9-12. International. Projects must address environmental issues.
cost: Application fee varies ($50-100); participation fee for finalists attending in person
aid: Limited scholarships available for qualifying students
notes: Held annually in June at RIT. CT Science & Engineering Fair provides pathways to this competition. Environmental/biology focus aligns well with interests. Good alternative for project-based students.

name: Research Science Institute (RSI)
eligibility: High school juniors only (rising seniors). U.S. citizens and international students. Must demonstrate exceptional academic achievement and research potential.
cost: Free for all admitted students (including travel, room, board, tuition)
aid: Full scholarship; no cost to attend
notes: Hosted at MIT. 6-week program. Combines STEM coursework with mentored research. Students produce conference-style oral and written research reports. Applications open in October. Requires standardized test scores (PSAT, SAT, ACT, or AP), teacher recommendations, essays, and transcript.
source: Center for Excellence in Education (CEE) website

name: Summer Science Program (SSP)
deadline: Late January/early February (typically Feb 1 for priority; rolling thereafter)
eligibility: High school sophomores and juniors (rising juniors and seniors). Must be at least 15 by program start. No citizenship restrictions.
cost: $7,950 (varies by campus); includes tuition, room, board, all activities
aid: Need-based financial aid available; approximately 60% of students receive aid. Full aid possible. Need-blind admissions.
notes: Offers multiple tracks: Astrophysics (Purdue, CU Boulder, Univ of Colorado), Biochemistry (Indiana Univ), Bacterial Genomics (Indiana Univ), Synthetic Chemistry, Cell Biology. Students work in teams of 3. Program runs mid-June through late July. Founded in 1959.

name: RISE (Research Internship in Science and Engineering)
eligibility: Rising high school seniors (current juniors). Must be at least 16 by program start. Strong academic record in science and math.
cost: $5,600 (Practicum track); Internship track: $5,500 (commuter) or $8,300 (residential). Includes tuition and fees.
aid: Need-based financial aid available. Merit-based scholarships possible. Submit financial aid application by deadline.
notes: 6-week program at Boston University. Internship track: individual lab placement with 1-on-1 mentoring. Practicum track: small group computational/neurobiology research. Both require faculty recommendation, transcript, essays. Program dates: late June - early August.

name: Stanford Institutes of Medicine Summer Research Program (SIMR)
eligibility: High school juniors and seniors (rising seniors preferred). Must be at least 16 by program start. Must live within commuting distance of Stanford (no housing provided).
aid: Need-based stipend available (up to $500). Program is free for all participants. No cost to apply or attend.
notes: 10-week program at Stanford University. 8 research areas: Cancer Biology, Cardiovascular Biology, Neuroscience, Bioengineering, Stem Cell & Regenerative Medicine, Immunology, Genetics/Bioinformatics, and Microbiology/Infectious Disease. Selection based on academic record, essays, and research interest. ~50 students admitted annually.

name: NIH High School Summer Internship Program (HS-SIP)
eligibility: Rising high school seniors (current juniors). Must be at least 17 by June 15. U.S. citizenship or permanent residency required. Must live within 40 miles of NIH campus or arrange own housing.
aid: Paid internship; stipend provided. Amount varies but typically $3,000-$4,000 for 8 weeks. Some commuting subsidies available.
notes: 8-week program at NIH main campus in Bethesda, MD (also available at NIEHS in NC, NIDA in Baltimore, etc.). Students are paid as federal employees. Must submit transcript, recommendation letters, and essays. Program runs June-August. Highly competitive.; [DEAD: https://www.training.nih.gov/programs/high-school-summer-internship-program]
source: NIH Office of Intramural Training & Education website

name: Garcia Summer Scholars
eligibility: High school juniors (rising seniors). Minimum 3.5 GPA. Strong background in science and math. Must complete prerequisite online course before program start.
cost: $7,700 (residential); $5,200 (commuter). Includes tuition, room, board for residential.
aid: Limited need-based financial aid available. Some merit scholarships. Submit financial aid application separately.
notes: 7-week program at Stony Brook University, NY. Focus on polymer science and materials research. Students write a research paper and present at symposium. Prerequisite: online course in polymer science. Many alumni publish in scientific journals. Program dates: late June - mid August.
source: Stony Brook University Garcia Center website

name: Rockefeller University Summer Science Research Program (SSRP)
eligibility: Rising high school seniors (current juniors). Must be at least 16 by program start. Must live within commuting distance of NYC (no housing). U.S. citizens or permanent residents.
aid: Free program; no cost to attend. Stipend of $3,000-$4,000 provided to participants. Commuting support available.
notes: 7-week program at Rockefeller University in New York City. Students are matched with a mentor lab. Research areas include molecular biology, genetics, neuroscience, biochemistry, and immunology. Program ends with a symposium where students present posters. Program runs late June - mid August.

name: Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory (CSHL) DNA Learning Center Summer Courses
deadline: Rolling; typically March for summer courses. Early application recommended.
eligibility: High school students; specific prerequisites vary by course. Some courses require prior biology and chemistry. Age 14+.
cost: $1,500 - $3,000 per course (varies by program). Some programs are full-day, multi-week.
aid: Limited need-based scholarships available. Some programs offer financial aid based on demonstrated need.
notes: Multiple course offerings include: DNA Barcoding, Human Genomics, Bacterial Genomics, BioInfo Summer. Located at CSHL in Laurel Hollow, NY (Long Island). Day program only - no residential option. Courses range from 1-4 weeks. Excellent lab experience for college applications.

name: Jackson Laboratory Summer Student Program (SSP)
eligibility: High school juniors and seniors (rising seniors preferred). Must be at least 16 by program start. Strong academic background in biology and math.
aid: Students receive a stipend (~$6,000). Housing and meals provided free of charge. Travel reimbursement available.
notes: 10-week program at JAX in Bar Harbor, Maine. Research focus on mammalian genetics, genomics, and computational biology. Students present research at poster session. Free housing in JAX dormitories. Program runs June-August.

name: Clark Scholar Program
eligibility: High school juniors (rising seniors). Minimum 3.5 GPA. Strong SAT/ACT scores. Must be at least 15 by program start.
aid: Free room and board on campus. Students receive a $750 stipend. No cost to apply or attend.
notes: 7-week residential program at Texas Tech University in Lubbock, TX. Students choose from any research area (biology, engineering, law, humanities, etc.). Includes a mentorship component, college prep workshops, and research presentations. One of the most competitive free summer programs.; [DEAD: https://www.depts.ttu.edu/honors/academics/enrichment/]
source: Texas Tech University Honors College website

name: MITES (MIT Introduction to Technology, Engineering, and Science)
eligibility: Rising high school seniors (current juniors). U.S. citizens/permanent residents. Strong academic record. Interest in STEM. Special consideration for underrepresented/minority backgrounds.
aid: Program is completely free including tuition, room, board, transportation, and books/technology fees.
notes: 6-week residential program at MIT. Students take 5 courses in math, science, engineering, and humanities. Also includes career exploration and college admissions prep. Highly competitive (~5% acceptance rate). Program runs June-July.; [DEAD: https://oge.mit.edu/programs/mites/]
source: MIT Office of Graduate Education website

name: Harvard Secondary School Program (SSP)
deadline: Early Decision: January; Regular Decision: February; Late: April (rolling)
eligibility: Current high school students entering grades 11-12 (rising juniors and seniors). Must be at least 16 by program start. Strong academic record (B+ or higher recommended).
cost: $3,700-$13,000 depending on number of courses (2-week to 7-week options). Residential fee: ~$14,000 for full session.
aid: Need-based financial aid available. Limited partial scholarships. Need-blind admissions for financial aid applicants.
notes: Two session lengths: 2-week Pre-College Program (non-credit) or 7-week Secondary School Program (college credit). Students live in Harvard dorms. Over 200 courses available. Prestigious experience. Program runs June-August.

name: Stanford Pre-Collegiate Studies (SPCS)
deadline: Rolling; January-March (varies by program). Summer Session typically January deadline.
eligibility: Current high school freshmen through juniors (varies by program). Summer Session: rising juniors/seniors, minimum 3.5 GPA. Summer Institutes: grades 9-11.
cost: $4,000-$15,000 depending on program. Summer Session (8-9 weeks, with housing): ~$15,000+. Summer Institutes (2-3 weeks): $3,000-$5,000.
aid: Need-based financial aid available for Summer Session. Limited aid for Summer Institutes. Submit financial aid application by deadline.
notes: Multiple programs: Summer Session (8-9 weeks, college credit), Summer Institutes (2-3 weeks, non-credit, focused topics), Summer Humanities Institute (residential). All held at Stanford University. Highly competitive admissions for credit program.

name: Brown Pre-College Programs
deadline: Rolling admission; early applications encouraged. Priority: February; Regular: March-April.
eligibility: Current high school students entering grades 9-12. Minimum age 14-15 depending on program. Strong academic record.
cost: $2,500-$4,500 per session (varies by length). Housing/meals additional (~$2,500). Full 3-week residential: ~$5,800-$6,800.
aid: Need-based financial aid available. Submit application early for consideration. Limited full scholarships.
notes: Multiple 1-4 week sessions in June-August. Courses in biology, neuroscience, law, political science, and more. Students live in Brown dorms. Very popular for college prep experience. Certificate of completion provided.

name: Cornell Pre-College Summer Programs
deadline: Rolling; early application recommended. Priority: February; Final: May (if space available).
eligibility: Current high school sophomores and juniors (rising juniors and seniors). Must be at least 15 by program start. Strong academic record (B+ or higher recommended).
cost: 3-week course: $5,400; 6-week course: $10,300+. Includes tuition, room, and meals.
aid: Limited need-based financial aid available. Some diversity scholarships. Submit financial aid application by January.
notes: Multiple 3-6 week sessions in June-August. College credit earned. Courses in Biology, Animal Science, Law & Society, Government, Engineering, and more. Includes college admissions workshops. Highly regarded.

name: Johns Hopkins Pre-College Summer Programs
deadline: Rolling; Priority: January/February; Final: May (space permitting).
eligibility: Current high school students (grades 9-12 depending on program). Must be 14-15+ depending on program. Strong academic record.
cost: Varies: 2-week Mini-Term $3,500; 5-week university credit program $12,000+. Includes tuition; housing/meals additional.
aid: Need-based financial aid available. Submit by priority deadline. Limited full scholarships.
notes: Multiple programs: Summer University (college credit), Mini-Term (non-credit exploration), Biomedical Engineering Innovation (research-focused). Located at JHU Homewood campus in Baltimore, MD. Strong reputation in pre-med and STEM.
source: Johns Hopkins University Summer Programs website

name: Yale Summer Session (YSS)
deadline: Rolling; Priority: January; Regular: April; Late: May (space permitting).
eligibility: Current high school students entering grades 10-12 (rising juniors and seniors). Must be at least 16 by program start. Strong academic record.
cost: 1 course (1 credit): $5,400; Full session: $10,000+. Residential: add $4,000+ for room and meals.
aid: Need-based financial aid available. Submit financial aid application by priority deadline. Limited scholarships.
notes: 5-week session (late June - early August) or two 3-week sessions. Wide range of courses including biology, molecular biology, law, political science, and more. College credit earned. Students live in Yale dorms.

name: Wharton Global Youth Program (Law & Business)
deadline: Priority: January; Regular: March; Rolling thereafter (space permitting).
eligibility: Current high school sophomores and juniors (grades 10-11). Minimum 3.5 GPA recommended. Strong English proficiency for international students.
cost: Varies: 2-week program $5,999+; 3-week $8,000+. Includes tuition, room, board, activities.
aid: Need-based financial aid available. Submit by priority deadline. Limited number of full scholarships. Need-blind admissions.
notes: Multiple programs at University of Pennsylvania. Law track includes Legal Research and Writing, Moot Court, and Law & Society courses. Business tracks include entrepreneurship, finance, and leadership programs. Highly prestigious. Program runs June-August.

name: Georgetown Law Summer High School Program
deadline: Rolling; typically March-May (space permitting). Early application recommended.
eligibility: Current high school sophomores and juniors (rising juniors/seniors). Minimum 3.0 GPA. Interest in law and government.
aid: Limited need-based financial aid available. Submit financial aid application by deadline.
notes: 1-2 week program at Georgetown University Law Center in Washington, DC. Covers legal reasoning, constitutional law, criminal law, and trial advocacy. Includes visits to courts and government buildings. Great for pre-law interest.

name: Harvard Pre-College Program (Law Track)
deadline: Early: January; Regular: February/March; Late: April (rolling, space permitting).
eligibility: Current high school sophomores and juniors (rising juniors/seniors). Must be at least 16 by program start. Strong academic record.
cost: $5,550 for 2-week session (includes tuition, room, board, activities). Application fee: $50.
aid: Need-based financial aid available. Covers full tuition for qualified students. Submit by early deadline. Need-blind admissions.
notes: 2-week non-credit program at Harvard University. Multiple sessions in June, July, and August. Law course offerings include: Constitutional Law, Legal Reasoning, Justice & Ethics, and Law & Society. Students choose 1-2 courses. Includes college prep workshops.

name: Telluride Association Summer Program (TASP)
eligibility: High school juniors (current 11th graders). No GPA or test score minimums. Emphasis on intellectual curiosity, writing ability, and diverse perspectives.
aid: Program is completely free. All costs (tuition, room, board, books, activities) covered. Stipend provided for travel expenses.
notes: 6-week program at Cornell University or University of Michigan. Seminar-style discussions on political theory, ethics, law, and social justice. No grades or credits - purely intellectual enrichment. Highly prestigious and selective (~5% acceptance rate).
